body:
# [Bug] MiniMax sparse-attention prefill: out-of-bounds GPU write when `max_seqlen_k` < `seq_lens.max()` (silent topk corruption / Xid 31 / NCCL watchdog worker kills)

## Summary

`flash_prefill_with_topk_index` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/minimax_sparse_ops/prefill/flash_with_topk_idx.py`)
allocates its `score` buffer from the **caller-provided `max_seqlen_k` int**, but the fwd/topk
kernels index that buffer per-sequence with widths computed from the **live `seq_lens` tensor**.
Nothing enforces `max_seqlen_k >= seq_lens.max()`. When the invariant breaks (stale forward
metadata — the backend snapshots `self._max_seqlen_k = int(forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu.max().item())`
at metadata-init time while the kernels read `forward_batch.seq_lens` live; these can diverge under
overlap scheduling / mixed chunking), the kernel's block-pointer stores run **past the allocation**.

Consequences, observed in production serving of MiniMax-M3 on GB200 (TP=4):
- **Common case — silent corruption**: the OOB write lands in adjacent allocator-pool memory and the
  topk block selection is computed from garbage → wrong sparse attention → degraded/garbage output,
  undetected.
- **Unlucky case — Xid 31 "GPU memory page fault"**: the write escapes mapped memory; the poisoned
  context hangs the next device→host sync, the rank misses its TP ALLREDUCE, and the NCCL watchdog
  (`ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp ... "taking the entire process down"`) kills the worker. We saw **~16
  worker kills / 40 h across a 24-worker fleet**, py-spy/faulthandler stacks 5/5 identical inside
  `flash_prefill_with_topk_index → get_cu_seqblocks`.

Verified present at current `main` (fetched 2026-07-13): allocation at
`prefill/flash_with_topk_idx.py:475-485`, live-width store at `:135` + `:145-147`
(`tl.make_block_ptr(shape=(q_len, block_num))` — `boundary_check` clamps to the *declared*
`block_num`, not the allocation), snapshot producer at `minimax_sparse_backend.py:178` vs live
tensor at `:307`.

## Deterministic reproduction (verbatim `main` code, GB200/SM100)

Two calls, identical inputs, only `max_seqlen_k` differs (correct 4096 vs stale 64; batch
`seq_lens=[64, 4096]`, per-rank MiniMax-M3 sparse params: 1 idx head × dim 128, `block_size_k=128`,
`topk=16`):

```
reference (correct): max_seqlen_k=4096 -> topk_idx (1, 4160, 16)
stale     (prod-bug): max_seqlen_k=64  -> topk_idx (1, 4160, 16)
corrupted topk indices: 42783 / 66560 total (all in the overrunning sequence's rows)
```

`compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` (required — under the
caching allocator the whole pool is one `cudaMalloc`, so the intra-pool overrun is invisible to
memcheck) captures the write directly:

```
Invalid __global__ write of size 4 bytes
    at _flash_attn_fwd_with_block_score_kernel+0x7110 in flash_with_topk_idx.py:236
    by thread (127,0,0) in block (31,1,0)
    Access to 0xf71cadfe8700 is out of bounds
    and is 1 bytes after the nearest allocation at 0xf71cadfe4600 of size 16,640 bytes
```

(16,640 B = exactly the stale-sized buffer: 1 head × 4,160 rows × 1 block-column × fp32; the write
is in k-block 31 — the column a correctly-sized 32-column buffer would contain.)

## Fix (one file, validated)

Derive the buffer width from the same tensor the kernels index, warn + enlarge when the caller's
value would undersize it — a strict no-op when the invariant holds (the path is eager prefill and
already host-syncs in `get_cu_seqblocks`, so the added `seq_lens.max().item()` is benign):

See attached `0001-fix-msa-score-buffer-oob.patch`. With the patch, the stale call above logs

```
flash_prefill_with_topk_index: max_seqlen_k=64 underestimates max(seq_lens)=4096; enlarging score
buffer from 1 to 32 block-columns to prevent an out-of-bounds write
```

and returns **bit-exact** output (0/66,560 mismatches). Regression test included
(`test_minimax_sparse_score_width.py`).

Note this guard hardens the kernel; the underlying metadata divergence
(`_max_seqlen_k` snapshot vs live `seq_lens` in `minimax_sparse_backend.py`) is arguably worth
fixing at the source as well — the warning added here gives direct telemetry on how often it fires.

## Environment
GB200 (SM100), TP=4, MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 + fp8 KV, `--enable-mixed-chunk --chunked-prefill-size 8192`,
overlap scheduler on. Bug is data/timing-dependent in serving; the repro above is deterministic by
injecting the stale value directly.
title: [Bug] MiniMax sparse prefill: OOB GPU write when max_seqlen_k < seq_lens.max() (silent topk corruption / Xid 31 / NCCL watchdog kills)
